items.title: Husband and wife living in same house but different rooms not cruelty by itself: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that merely occupying separate rooms in the same premises does not, by itself, constitute matrimonial cruelty. A Bench of Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan said that such separation can assume significance when viewed alongside the broader matrimonial history of a couple. The Court noted that the husband in this case himself had admitted that the parties had occupied separate rooms for a considerable period. “Standing by itself, such an arrangement cannot be treated as cruelty. The mere fact that spouses occupy separate rooms, without anything more, would not justify a finding of cruelty." It held that the separation could not be viewed in isolation and formed part of a prolonged matrimonial history involving repeated disputes, allegations of abuse, estrangement, an earlier matrimonial proceeding and the eventual failure of the relationship. The Court made the observation while dismissing an appeal filed by a man against a family court verdict which dissolved his marriage with his wife on the ground of cruelty and directed him to pay permanent alimony of ₹25,000 per month.
